rules.statement: API resources and DTOs that represent a secret or key expose only metadata (use, algorithm, type, size, created/expiry times) and never the encoded or protected key material.
rules.why: No public API may return key material; keeping secret resources metadata-only keeps key material from crossing the API boundary.
rules.check: Look for response models or mappings that include an encoded value, PEM, raw key bytes or protected payload of a secret.

rules.statement: Create secret key material on the server from requested metadata (type, key size) and do not accept raw private or symmetric key material in management API requests unless a separate decision approves import.
rules.why: Importing keys puts plaintext private key material on the wire and in operator tooling. Generating keys on the server keeps the private key inside the protection boundary from the start.
rules.check: Look for create or update request DTOs or endpoints that take key material (encoded value, PEM, key bytes) to store as a secret, including on owner-creation endpoints.

rules.statement: Treat a secret's key material as immutable after creation: update operations change only metadata such as expiry, use and algorithm, and rotation creates a new secret with a new id rather than replacing material under an existing id.
rules.why: Replacing key material silently under a stable secret id makes rotation ambiguous: tokens signed by the old key still look valid by id but fail verification. Immutable material keeps rotation auditable.
rules.check: Look for update/PUT/PATCH paths that overwrite a persisted secret's encoded value or key material in place.

rules.statement: Any code that writes protected secret material must protect and encode it with the same protector or key mechanism that the matching read path uses to unprotect it, and that logic belongs next to its inverse in the secrets package, not in consuming layers.
rules.why: Writing must be the exact reverse of reading. Doing it in management layers duplicates the protect/encode logic and pulls crypto dependencies into them.
rules.check: Look for secret persistence that stores unprotected material, uses a protector different from the read path, or reimplements protect/encode/key generation inside API or management projects.

rules.statement: Put generation of new key material behind its own dedicated contract instead of adding it to a serializer whose job is encoding and decoding existing material.
rules.why: Generating new keys is a separate concern from encoding and decoding existing material, so it needs its own contract.
rules.check: Look for key-generation methods added to serializer or encoder interfaces.

rules.statement: Store methods that add, update or remove an individual secret must also bump the owning entity's secrets concurrency token, so cached secret providers refresh.
rules.why: Running secret providers find out about changes through the owner's secrets concurrency token. If it is not bumped, they keep serving stale keys.
rules.check: Look for per-secret add/update/remove store methods that do not update the owner's secrets concurrency token.

rules.statement: When an entity loaded by id does not carry its owning tenant, wrap it in an owner-scoped resource that carries a tenant id from a trustworthy owner-scoped lookup before running resource-based authorization.
rules.why: Tenant-scoped authorization handlers only evaluate resources that carry a tenant id. Authorizing the bare entity drops scoped admins to the global-admin-only path.
rules.check: Look for resource-based authorization calls that pass an entity without tenant information in a tenant-scoped context, or that take the tenant id from an untrusted source instead of the owner-scoped query.

rules.statement: Check uniqueness and parent existence in a validator before the write, returning 409 Conflict for duplicates and 400 Bad Request for a missing parent, instead of inferring them from a caught store exception.
rules.why: Checking first gives a deterministic status code and response body.
rules.check: Look for create handlers that catch database or unique-constraint exceptions to detect duplicates or missing parents.

rules.statement: Assign the row concurrency token eagerly on insert, so a 201 Created response can return a correct ETag without reading the entity again.
rules.why: Without it, POST would need an extra read to produce a correct ETag.
rules.check: Look for create endpoints that re-query the entity after insert just to get its concurrency token, or that return an ETag before the token is assigned.

rules.statement: Guard deletion of an entity that still has dependents: the validator rejects it with 409 Conflict, and the store's remove method checks the same invariant again, unless a decision explicitly makes that delete cascade.
rules.why: This keeps removal a leaf-only operation even if a caller bypasses the endpoint.
rules.check: Look for delete endpoints or store remove methods for owner entities that skip the dependents check in either the validator or the store.

rules.statement: Mark deliberately deferred functionality with a `// Future:` comment at the place where it would go, and do not add a partial implementation.
rules.why: Deferred features such as key import need their own review. The note marks where the additive change would go without shipping unreviewed code.
rules.check: Look for half-implemented deferred features, or extension points for planned features that lack a `// Future:` note.
